newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Flemish region interested in Tractebel.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Flemish region interested in Tractebel.

text.p: Flanders, Belgium's northern Dutch-speaking region, is interested in helping Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) partially re-place shares in utility holding company Tractebel SA, the Flemish government said on Wednesday.

"There is interest from the Flemish government in the Tractebel group, but there have been no direct talks with SGB and (its French parent company) Suez," Herman Daems, chief of staff of Flemish Economics Minister Eric Van Rompuy, told Belgian BRTN radio.
He added this should not lead to a partial nationalisation.

Asked whether Flemish public holding company GIMV could take a stake in Tractebel, Daems said: "I think it is up to Flemish entrepreneurs and financiers to show their interest now, the GIMV can play a role in that, but we do not want a kind of nationalisation of Tractebel."

On Tuesday SGB said it planned to boost its stake in Tractebel to 65 percent from 40 percent by acquiring all Tractebel shares held by Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert SA (GBL) and its affiliates.
Tractebel and Flanders have long had a prickly relationship because of the perceived French influence on Tractebel.
